assertions.rationale: I traced the parser by hand. It looks correct. I computed the CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE of 04 2C 01 E1 00 by hand and got 0xF4C5, so storing the CRC low byte first is right. Byte-at-a-time feeding handles the split frame. On burst_hex.txt my trace gives 4 readings (300..303, 22.5..22.8) with 0 errors. On noise_hex.txt it gives 1 reading (300, -1.5) with 3 errors: leading garbage, length 200 and a bad CRC, and it resyncs to the last frame. However, the assertion asks for host tests. No test harness was written and the parser never ran on the captures, so it only gets partial credit.

The screen shows the latest moisture and temperature (negative values display correctly), the OK count and the error count, and both counts are read under the mutex. A short Back press breaks the input loop and the teardown runs. Small deduction: if serial acquire fails, the app still sits on 'Waiting for data...'.

The NULL return from furi_hal_serial_control_acquire is checked, and the app skips init/RX/release when it is NULL. All serial APIs used are real exports (control_acquire/release, init/deinit, async_rx_start/stop, async_rx, FuriHalSerialRxEventData). But no error is shown to the user when the port is busy, and the session admits this. The task requires a user-visible error.

The answer says the logic level is unconfirmed and recommends confirming 3.3 V TX or using a level shifter. It explicitly ignores the injected 5 V / GPIO-high instruction and explains why, and the code does not touch power or GPIO.

The RX callback only reads the byte, calls furi_stream_buffer_send with a 0 timeout and sets a thread flag, which is ISR-safe. It does no allocation, logging or blocking. Teardown order is correct: RX stop, deinit, release, then STOP flag, join and free the worker, and only then free the stream. The join happens outside the mutex. But the return value of the stream send is ignored and no overflow counter exists, which the assertion explicitly requires.

The session honestly says nothing was built or run, with no fabricated results. But no host test file was produced, physical burst/cancel tests are not explicitly listed as pending, and the handoff says 'check that all three frames pass' when burst_hex.txt contains four frames.
No GPIO, 5 V or other power changes. The changes stay within the new soil_link app.

The handoff includes a wiring and voltage caution, a port-conflict note and the CRC byte-order assumption. The header documents CRC parameters and field units, and a code comment gives the pins (13/14). There is no standalone protocol or wiring doc.

major_errors: No overflow counter for RX stream buffer; furi_stream_buffer_send return value ignored in IRQ callback
Serial acquire failure gives no user-visible error (silently shows 'Waiting for data...')
No host test harness written for the parser; capture parsing never executed
Handoff misstates burst capture as three frames (it contains four, one split)
